bugs.text: collide() dereferences player.dual while player is null (hitPlayer sets player=null and respawns 900 ms later via setTimeout). The TypeError escapes update() and loop() never re-arms requestAnimationFrame, so the game freezes permanently on the first death. Confirmed by result.json (pageerror 'reading dual') and the identical screenshots at 5 s, 8 s, 30 s, 60 s.

e.slotY is never assigned (only slotX). Enemies that finish the entry path get y=undefined, so the formation is never drawn and cannot be hit; dives start from NaN and are invisible, never fire and never end. The stage can never be cleared.

All 30 enemies enter at the same instant and pathIdx advances 150 path points per second over a 41-point path: the entire entry takes ~0.3 s, with no groups, then the enemies vanish (previous bug). The only real play is dodging the ~10 bullets the entering enemies spray.
The canvas is sized W*scale but the 2D context is never scaled, so the whole game renders at 1x (224x288 px) in the top-left corner of a large black canvas, not scaled or centred.

Challenging stage: only one wave of 8 is ever spawned; wrapX keeps x inside the screen so enemies never become 'gone'; dead enemies are never removed so enemies.length never hits 0; and `challengeResult` is assigned without declaration under 'use strict' (ReferenceError). challengeData is also never reset for later stages, so F1 would stop advancing after stage 3.
The tractor beam, capture, rescue and dual fighter can never trigger: tryCapture needs a diving boss with 80<y<175 and diving y is always NaN.
Formation has 30 enemies (4 boss, 12 Goei, 14 Zako) instead of 40 (4/16/20).
Wing-flap frame `flap` is computed but never used; sprites do not animate.
A single fighter always fires two side-by-side bullets per press and shotsFired counts 2, halving the hit ratio.
Boss Galaga is scored on its first hit (award before return) and again when destroyed: double points.
Dead enemies stay in `enemies` (alive=false) and are still eligible as divers, counted as formation members and as 'escorts' for boss scoring; invisible dead divers could fire.
Only one stage flag is drawn (colour by denomination), not the arcade's row of badges.
Dual fighter: a hit removes the whole player, not one half; captured fighter is drawn below the boss (227) rather than above.
Sound.enemyHit is defined but never called.
Pause stops updates but shows no PAUSED text; the frame keeps rendering unchanged.
Dives are allowed while player is null (between death and respawn) because the guard is `player && player.state!=='alive'`.

summary: The file is compact (254 lines) and shows the right skeleton: a fixed-step rAF loop, separated update/render, pixel-art sprite tables, a Web Audio sound object, bezier dives, a tractor-beam state machine and the full scoring table. But it is held together by one-line functions and global state and was clearly never run: the formation's y coordinate is never assigned (so the enemy fleet vanishes after a 0.3-second entry and nothing can be hit, dived or captured), the context is never scaled (the game sits unscaled in a corner), the challenge stage uses an undeclared variable, and the first player death throws on a null player and freezes the loop for good. What a player actually experiences is a nice title screen, a blur of enemies for a fraction of a second, a shower of bullets, then a frozen explosion. Almost nothing of Galaga's rhythm (entry groups, breathing formation, dives, beam, dual fighter, challenging stages) ever appears on screen, so despite the paper-level fidelity of the constants it does not feel like Galaga at all.
